documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
53 y/o man, former construction worker, transferring primary care. Here to set up and get his preventive care sorted.

RA: seropositive, erosive, diagnosed spring 2022 by an outside rheumatology group, who he keeps seeing every few months. On methotrexate 15 mg once a week (six 2.5 mg tabs, takes them Sunday nights), folic acid daily, prednisone 5 mg daily since diagnosis. Calcium and vitamin D for the steroid. Hands are stiff for about an hour on waking, manageable most days. Went on disability from the building trades because he can't grip tools for a full shift.

TB: had pulmonary TB in his early thirties, around 2004. Says he took pills for six months through the health department and was told he was cured. No records of that.

Asbestos: decades of demolition and renovation work, often around old insulation and pipe wrap, rarely with a mask.

Tobacco: 30 pack-years, stopped in June, about two months ago. No patch or meds, just quit. Alcohol: drank heavily for years, he calls it a long-term problem. Stopped at the same time. Not in a program. No withdrawal symptoms now, no cravings he can't manage.

Family: father COPD, mother thyroid disease (autoimmune), brother lung cancer.
Allergies: none to medications.
No surgeries.

ROS: no cough, fevers, sweats or weight loss. No dyspnea. No GI symptoms.

Exam: BP and vitals as recorded. Large man, comfortable. Lungs clear throughout, no crackles. Heart regular, no murmur. Abdomen soft, no hepatomegaly. Hands: boggy synovial thickening over several MCPs on both sides, mild tenderness, full fist possible but slow. Wrists without effusion. No nodules. Skin unremarkable.

A/P:
1. RA - on MTX/folate/pred per rheum. CBC and CMP today, we can share the monitoring draws with rheum.
2. Remote TB, treated. Noted.
3. Former tobacco, 30 pack-years, quit 2 mo ago. Eligible for lung screening; ordered LDCT. Congratulated on quitting.
4. Alcohol use disorder, early remission. AUDIT-C 0 since June. Offered counseling resources, he declines for now.
5. Obesity, BMI 35.5. Discussed.
6. Chronic prednisone - DXA ordered, on calcium/D. Vitamin D level today.
7. HM: Tdap today. Lipids, A1c, hep C screen. Will request prior records for colonoscopy date. Flu/COVID/pneumococcal/shingles at a nurse visit in early October.

RTC 3-4 months.

Cholesterol is acceptable, A1c 5.6 (no diabetes), hepatitis C screen negative, vitamin D 34 which is fine on your current supplement. No changes. The CT and bone density scheduling desk should call you this week.

Visit date: 09/07/2023
Re: Craig Roy, DOB 05/19/1970

Dear colleague,

Thank you for taking over Mr. Roy's primary care. I saw him for his regular follow-up of seropositive erosive rheumatoid arthritis. He describes morning stiffness of about an hour and intermittent MCP swelling. On examination today there was mild synovitis at both second and third MCPs.

Medications: methotrexate 15 mg weekly, folic acid 1 mg daily, prednisone 5 mg daily, calcium carbonate 600 mg twice daily, vitamin D3 2000 IU daily.

With regards,
Rheumatology

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - MEDICINE SERVICE
Admitted 08/09/2024, discharged 08/17/2024
Patient: Craig Roy, 54 M

Principal diagnosis: Pulmonary tuberculosis, recurrent, smear positive, with right upper lobe cavity.

History: 54-year-old man with seropositive erosive RA and pulmonary TB treated in the early 2000s, started on etanercept by his rheumatologist roughly eight weeks ago in addition to methotrexate and prednisone. He came in with three weeks of fevers, drenching night sweats, productive cough, weight loss and fatigue.

On arrival: T 38.6 C, HR 102, RR 22, BP 128/76, SpO2 94% on room air. Obese, BMI 34, weight 107.7 kg. Crackles throughout both lung fields.

Chest film: patchy bilateral upper-lobe opacities and a 3.2 cm thick-walled right upper lobe cavity.

Microbiology: sputum AFB smear positive on all three induced specimens. MTB complex PCR detected, no rifampin resistance mutation. Cultures pending at discharge. HIV Ag/Ab nonreactive.

Hospital course: placed in airborne isolation on arrival. Etanercept discontinued. Health department TB program notified. Four-drug therapy started 08/10: isoniazid 300 mg, rifampin 600 mg, pyrazinamide 2000 mg, ethambutol 1600 mg daily, with pyridoxine 50 mg. Tolerated without nausea or rash. Baseline liver tests normal. Fevers resolved by day 5. Methotrexate, folic acid and prednisone continued after discussion with his rheumatologist.

Discharge medications: isoniazid 300 mg daily, rifampin 600 mg daily, pyrazinamide 2000 mg daily, ethambutol 1600 mg daily, pyridoxine 50 mg daily (all via TB program DOT); methotrexate 15 mg weekly; folic acid 1 mg daily; prednisone 5 mg daily; calcium carbonate 600 mg twice daily; vitamin D3 2000 IU daily.
STOPPED: etanercept.
Allergies: NKDA.

Disposition: home with home isolation until cleared by the TB program. DOT through the health department starts 08/18. Follow up with PCP within one week (video is fine while isolated) and with rheumatology.

documents.title: Call from hospital case manager
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Case manager from the regional hospital called: our patient admitted 8/9 with active pulmonary TB, smear positive, in isolation, started on four-drug treatment. Health dept involved. Expected discharge later this week; they want a PCP follow-up within 7 days, video ok since he'll be on home isolation. Message to PCP. Will book once discharge date is known.

Video, pt at home on home isolation per TB program. Identity verified.

Discharged 8/17 after admission for recurrent pulmonary TB, cavitary, smear positive, about 8 weeks after starting etanercept. Discharge summary reviewed.

Now: no fever since the hospital. Cough still there but less sputum. Sleeping through without soaking the sheets. Appetite coming back. Health dept nurse comes daily for DOT, has had no missed doses. Orange urine, knows it's the rifampin. No nausea, no yellowing, no rash, no vision change.

Meds reconciled: INH 300, rifampin 600, PZA 2000, ethambutol 1600, B6 50 daily via DOT; MTX 15 weekly; folate; pred 5; calcium; D3. Etanercept off.

A/P:
1. Pulmonary TB, recurrent, on RIPE via health dept. Agree with plan; they manage dosing and cultures. Reviewed liver warning signs and to stop drinking entirely (he already has). He asked whether the Enbrel caused this - told him it likely allowed old TB to wake up, and that rheumatology will need a non-TNF option later.
2. RA on MTX/pred, biologic stopped. Rheum aware.
In-person visit once the TB program clears him from isolation. LFTs then.

Patient: Craig Roy, 56 M

HPI: Four days of productive cough, fevers with chills, shortness of breath and sharp right-sided chest pain on deep breaths. Has seropositive RA on rituximab infusions every six months plus methotrexate and prednisone. Treated pulmonary TB 2024-25. Former smoker, former heavy drinker, sober for three years. Long construction career with asbestos exposure.

Triage: T 38.5 C, HR 108, RR 24, BP 118/72, SpO2 93% RA.
Exam: ill-appearing but conversant. Diminished breath sounds and crackles at the right base. Heart tachycardic, regular. No edema.

Results: WBC 13.6 with 84% neutrophils. BMP unremarkable. Blood cultures x2 drawn. Sputum sent for Gram stain and culture.
CXR: new right lower lobe consolidation; old RUL scarring unchanged.

Assessment: right lower lobe community-acquired pneumonia in an immunosuppressed patient. Imaging pattern not suggestive of TB recurrence. Observed in the ED, tolerating oral intake and walking without distress.

Disposition: discharged home. Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg twice daily for 10 days and azithromycin 500 mg today then 250 mg daily for 4 days. Hold methotrexate until the antibiotic course is complete. Continue prednisone. Return for worsening breathing, chest pain or persistent fever. See PCP within one week.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Pt call after ED visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called: was in the ED last night, told it's pneumonia in the right lung, sent home on two antibiotics. Has picked them up and taken first doses. Feels wiped out, still running a fever this morning, taking Tylenol, breathing ok at rest. Told to hold his methotrexate as the ED said. Reviewed when to go back. Booked post-ED visit 6/11, ED records requested.

Visit 06/03/2026
Sputum culture (collected 06/03) final 06/06: Streptococcus pneumoniae, penicillin susceptible. Covered by discharge regimen. Blood cultures no growth at 5 days. Patient notified by phone; no change in therapy.

documents.title: Office Visit - Post ED
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen in the regional ED 6/3 for RLL pneumonia. ED record and culture addendum reviewed: sputum grew pneumococcus, pen-sensitive; blood cultures negative.

Day 8 of 10 on amox-clav; azithro finished. Last fever Saturday. Cough looser, less of it, sputum now pale. Right-sided chest pain gone. Short of breath only on the stairs. Eating. Has been holding MTX since the ED as told. Still on pred 5.

Exam: afebrile, sat 97% RA, vitals as charted. A few crackles R base, otherwise clear. No dullness. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P:
1. Pneumococcal pneumonia RLL, improving on amox-clav (azithro done). Finish course. Repeat CBC today. Repeat PA/lat CXR in 6-8 wks to make sure it has cleared, given his smoking history and lung history; order placed.
2. RA on rituximab q6mo/MTX/pred. Keep MTX on hold until antibiotics are finished, then restart at the usual dose; message me when done. Rheum next course due Sept - will let them know about the pneumonia.
3. PCV20 given 2023. No further pneumococcal vaccine indicated now.
RTC September, sooner if fevers return.

documents.title: Done with antibiotics
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Took the last antibiotic pill Saturday night. Feeling pretty much normal, some cough in the morning. OK to go back on the methotrexate this Sunday?

documents.title: Re: Done with antibiotics
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, restart methotrexate at your usual 6 tablets this Sunday. Your blood count from the visit was back to normal. Remember the chest x-ray late July or early August.

documents.author: MA
documents.body: eRx request: prednisone 5 mg #90 and folic acid 1 mg #90. Seen 6/11. Approved per PCP standing refill plan, sent.

documents.body: Hi Craig, a reminder that the follow-up chest x-ray ordered in June hasn't been done yet. It's walk-in at the imaging center, no appointment needed.

documents.title: Re: Chest x-ray reminder

documents.body: Thanks, slipped my mind. Truck's in the shop, will get over there once it's back.
